run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: The logs requested for the incident window are not present. The `app-261-prod-logs` index holds only 4 documents in total at query time, and all 4 are INFO 'healthy' lines timestamped 17:02:50Z–17:27:50Z (after the reported incident), from services `checkout-service` and `payment-service` with `cluster: production-eu-west-2`. A search of the index filtered to 09:00:00Z–13:30:00Z on 2026-11-23 (covering the ~11:27Z 'six hours ago' point) returned zero documents, so this index cannot explain the checkout 500s. The Kubernetes side does not describe that window either: every otel-demo pod and ReplicaSet was created at 14:36–14:38Z on 2026-11-23 (about three hours ago), all 22 pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, all 24 deployments show 1/1 ready, and a grouped event query over all namespaces returned no events. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable throughout this Run (every call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, tried via get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query, and via traces_list_services and traces_search), so error-rate, latency and trace confirmation of the reported 500s is unknown. The only related configuration observation is a Prometheus alerting rule `CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh` (checkout PlaceOrder SERVER spans, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR ratio > 0.5 for 2m, severity critical, label cluster=opspilot-m1), which shows an alert definition matching the symptom but not whether or when it fired, and `flagd-config`'s fault-injection flags (including `paymentFailure` and `paymentUnreachable`) all read `defaultVariant: off` at query time. No root cause can be named from the available evidence; the change_history source is not integrated, so change activity around the incident is also unknown.

claims.text: The `app-261-prod-logs` index existed and held exactly 4 documents (health green, 6.7kb) at query time; no other index was returned by the wildcard index listing.

All 4 documents in `app-261-prod-logs` have `cluster: production-eu-west-2`, `level: INFO` and timestamps 2026-11-23T17:02:50Z, 17:12:50Z, 17:22:50Z and 17:27:50Z: 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' (checkout-service), 'All payment provider connections healthy' (payment-service), 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes' and 'Healthy: p95 latency 215ms' (checkout-service). Because the index total is 4 and every document lies in 17:02–17:27Z, none carries a timestamp in the ~11:27Z window the question describes.

The log documents' own `cluster` field reads `production-eu-west-2`, so the returned log data belongs to the cluster named in the question. The index's `service` values are `checkout-service` and `payment-service`, while the Prometheus alerting rule and Jaeger service naming use `service_name="checkout"` / `service_name="payment"`.

Current cluster state in namespace `otel-demo` postdates the incident: all 22 pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, and every pod's startTime is between 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and 14:38:04Z; the checkout pod is `checkout-6578865d87-v6flf` (container `checkout`, started 14:36:30Z, no previous instance). All 23 ReplicaSets, including `checkout-6578865d87` owned by Deployment `checkout`, were created in the same 14:36–14:38Z interval, and all 24 deployments report 1 ready / 1 available / 1 replica.

The Prometheus configuration in ConfigMap `prometheus` defines alerting rule `CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh` in group `opspilot-lab`: it fires when the ratio of error-ratio over total `traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}` exceeds 0.5 for 2m, with severity critical and label cluster=opspilot-m1. This is the rule definition as read at query time, not its firing state during the incident.

ConfigMap `flagd-config` (key `demo.flagd.json`) contains fault-injection flags relevant to payment and checkout paths — `paymentFailure` (variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off), `paymentUnreachable`, `cartFailure`, `productCatalogFailure`, `recommendationCacheFailure` — and at query time every one of them reads `defaultVariant: off`. This is the configuration state at query time only; it says nothing about the flag values in effect at ~11:27Z.

Candidate explanation: the checkout 500s / failed payments could have been produced by an injected payment-path fault (`paymentFailure` or `paymentUnreachable` in flagd-config) or by a genuine payment-service failure. Nothing in this Run confirms it: no log, span or metric sample from the ~11:27Z window was retrievable, Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and the flags read off only at 17:27Z after a full 14:36Z redeploy. Confirmation would need checkout/payment error logs or `traces_span_metrics_calls_total` / `rpc_*_duration` series covering 11:00–12:30Z and the flagd flag values in effect at that time.

Before attributing the incident, obtain a log source that actually covers 11:00–12:30Z on 2026-11-23 (this index holds only 4 post-incident documents) and re-check Prometheus/Jaeger availability so checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and payment RPC status can be measured; also read the alertmanager history for `CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh`.

gaps: No log data exists for the incident window in `app-261-prod-logs`: a search on time field `timestamp` from 2026-11-23T09:00:00Z to 13:30:00Z returned 0 documents (status no_data), and the index holds only 4 documents in total, all timestamped 17:02:50Z–17:27:50Z.

Prometheus was unreachable for the entire Run: get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout error rate, error ratios, latency and any ERROR series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search (service checkout, 10:30–12:30Z) both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error evidence or call chain for the incident exists in this Run.
Kubernetes events across all namespaces returned no items (total_items_processed 0, status no_data), so restarts, kills, evictions or rollouts during 11:00–12:30Z could not be observed.

Current Kubernetes objects cannot describe the incident: every pod and ReplicaSet was created at 14:36–14:38Z on 2026-11-23, so any earlier pod generation, its termination reason and its logs are unknown.

The current checkout pod's log stream (288 lines, current instance only, no previous container instance) contained no line matching error|fatal|fail|exception|panic|500 for the final hour, but that query covered only 16:27–17:27Z and returned no_data; the incident hour was not covered.

ConfigMap/flagd values were read at 17:27Z, after an environment redeploy at 14:36Z; the fault-flag values in effect at ~11:27Z are unknown, and secrets could not be read to verify anything credential-dependent.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, config or flag change history around the incident could be checked.
Alert firing history for `CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh` is unknown because the alertmanager/Prometheus API was unavailable; only the rule definition stored in ConfigMap `prometheus` was readable.
next_steps: Confirm the exact incident start/end timestamps and the workload identity (Deployment `checkout` in namespace `otel-demo` in cluster `production-eu-west-2`) from the P1 ticket, then query a log source that retains that period.

When Prometheus is reachable, evaluate the existing rule expression over 11:00–12:30Z to measure the checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and compare with a pre-incident baseline, and read `rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_service=~".*Payment.*"}` / grpc status codes for the payment dependency.
When Jaeger is reachable, pull checkout PlaceOrder traces in the incident window and follow parent references to the payment spans named in those traces.
Review alertmanager history and flagd flag-change audit for 11:00–12:30Z to determine whether `paymentFailure` / `paymentUnreachable` were switched on at the time.

Check whether the 14:36–14:38Z redeploy of all otel-demo workloads was the recovery action for this P1 and, if so, capture the pre-redeploy pod/ReplicaSet details from change history, which is not integrated here.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
","alerts":"{}

When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident.
